result:
This confirms the agent's findings against the actual source. Here's the full path.

**What starts the check.** Two triggers converge on the same job. An external caller can hit `POST` in `src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`, which checks a cron secret and calls `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())`. Internally, `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` runs a `tick()` every 60 seconds; once the `"overdue-issues"` job's 60‑minute cadence has elapsed, it enqueues that job kind, and `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` (around line 130) dispatches it to the same `runOverdueIssueJob` function in `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`.

**Narrowing the set of issues that count.** `runOverdueIssueJob` loops over org IDs (`usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup`) and, per org, calls `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, stamp)` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`. That query filters to the org, excludes archived issues, requires `dueAt` to be set and in the past, and restricts `status` to the still-open values (`backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, `in_review`) — so done/cancelled issues never count no matter how stale their due date.

**What the checking component does and doesn't do.** For each overdue issue not yet in its `reported` set, the job emits an `issue.overdue` domain event via `emit()` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, carrying `orgId`, `issueId`, `dueAt`, and `assigneeId`. The job's own doc comment is explicit: "The job owns no notification logic: it announces the fact, and whoever cares... reacts on the bus." It never touches email, in-app rows, or user preferences itself — that's fully delegated to event subscribers.

**Preventing repeat announcements.** Dedup is a plain in-memory `Set<string>` named `reported`, module-scoped in `overdue-issue-job.ts`. Before emitting, the job checks `if (reported.has(issue.id)) continue;`, and adds the id right after a successful `emit()`. This means dedup only lasts for the process's lifetime — a restart would re-announce still-overdue issues — and there's no persisted "already notified" column; the guarantee is "not announced twice by this running process," not a durable idempotency record.

**Reaching one specific person through their chosen channels.** `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` subscribes to `issue.overdue` at module load (`registerFanOut`). If `assigneeId` is null it drops the event; otherwise it calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [assigneeId], {...})`. `notify()` loads that user's row via `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "issue_overdue")` and passes it to `resolveChannels()`, which builds the channel list: `in_app` if `preference.inApp` is true, `email` if `preference.email` is true and either `digestOnly` is off or the org's `digest_email` flag is enabled. A user with no saved preference gets the default `["in_app", "email"]`; a user who has muted every channel resolves to an empty list and is skipped — no row is written for them at all. The surviving channel set is stored as a `channels` array on one row via `notificationRepo.insertNotifications`, which is what makes it appear in-app; the email leg isn't sent inline but picked up later by the digest job (`digest-email-job.ts`), which bundles unread notifications and sends them, then marks them read so the same overdue notice isn't re-sent in the next digest pass.
